answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: bind each identity to one scarce resource bought at market price, because oasis only stays cheap while the attacker's cost scales linearly with fleet size while payout per identity stays flat. Concretely, jade is enforced in the ledger: The network tolerates clones that do real work; it only refuses ones that add no signal. Any copper approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
